title: Harlem Run: Monday Night Run
description: Free, inclusive pacer-led runs and walks through Harlem, starting and ending at Marcus Garvey Park. Paces from 7 to 12 minutes per mile plus run/walk and walk groups; open to all ages and abilities, with bag drop available. Repeats every Monday through June 2027.
venue: Marcus Garvey Park, south side of Pelham Fritz Recreation Center, W 122nd St and Mount Morris Park West
fit_reason: A free weekly group run in Harlem with pacers for every pace - a standing Monday-night habit that costs nothing.

title: Queens Night Market
description: New York City's flagship night market takes over the grounds outside the New York Hall of Science in Flushing Meadows Corona Park with dozens of international food vendors, live performers, and a rotating weekly lineup. Doors run from 4 PM until midnight.
venue: New York Hall of Science, Flushing Meadows Corona Park
fit_reason: Dozens of international food stalls and performances in one Queens park on a Saturday night.

title: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
description: A monthlong celebration of memory, life, and renewal featuring marigold displays, a community ofrenda, calaveras, a flower-covered Catrina, weekend music and crafts, and a parade on November 1.
venue: New York Botanical Garden, 2900 Southern Boulevard
fit_reason: A substantial cultural celebration in the Bronx with botanical displays, art, music, crafts, and community traditions.

title: NYC Off-Broadway Week
description: NYC Tourism's biannual Off-Broadway promotion returns with 2-for-1 tickets, 50% off each seat, to participating Off-Broadway productions across the city; 25 shows are listed for the fall edition.
fit_reason: The cheapest reliable route into Off-Broadway all year: 2-for-1 seats booked with code OBW26.

title: Game-A-Palooza 2026
description: IGDA NYC's curated indie-game showcase opens its locally made and unreleased games to the public from 1 PM, with opportunities to play and meet New York developers.
fit_reason: Hands-on access to unreleased games and local developers for only $10.

title: New York Comic Con 2026
description: NYCC’s 20th-anniversary edition spans comics, anime, manga, science fiction, gaming, authors, cosplay, film, television, exhibitors, and creator appearances.
venue: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, 429 11th Avenue
price_label: Adult single-day Thursday tickets $103.98 including taxes and fees; Saturday, 4-day, and VIP passes sold out
fit_reason: A nearby convention bringing comics, manga, anime, science fiction, and gaming together.

title: Queer in Every Career: LGBTQ+ Career Fair 2026
description: The Center’s annual career fair connects LGBTQ+ job seekers with affirming NYC employers, networking, resume feedback, coaching, and skill-building workshops.
venue: The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual & Transgender Community Center, 208 W 13th Street
fit_reason: A queer community event with practical career-change support, workshops, and networking.

title: Horror and Dark Literature Book Club: The October Country
description: An in-person adult discussion of Ray Bradbury’s The October Country, focused on horror and dark literature.
fit_reason: A free adult book-club night for horror, dark fantasy, and classic science fiction readers.

title: Open House New York Weekend
description: Three days of behind-the-scenes access to more than 300 destinations across the five boroughs: new buildings reshaping the skyline, infrastructure facilities keeping the city running, performance spaces, parks, and manufacturing workshops. More than 150 sites are drop-in, while some sites and tours require tickets released October 2.
price_label: Free drop-in access at 150+ sites; some sites and tours require advance tickets
fit_reason: Behind-the-scenes architecture and infrastructure access across the city, from landmark civic buildings to the systems underneath them.

title: Field Conditions: Incubating Media Arts in NYC
description: A panel bringing together NEW INC at the New Museum, Rhizome, and Onassis ONX on how New York’s art, design, and technology institutions support practitioners, where funding and institutional models are heading, and what is emerging in computational design, interaction, and immersive media.
venue: Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, Tata Innovation Center, Cornell Tech, 11 East Loop Road, 4th Floor
fit_reason: A direct look at the institutions behind New York’s creative-technology scene, covering AI storytelling and immersive media.

title: Gallery Tours: A Few of Our Favorite Things
description: A free staff-led gallery tour through highlights of the Brooklyn Museum’s collection, offered on selected weekdays and Sundays.
fit_reason: A free guided museum tour in Prospect Heights, easy to pair with the museum’s current shows.

title: Piano in Bryant Park
description: Open-air piano performances on the Upper Terrace in Bryant Park, free to stop by over the lunch hour.
fit_reason: A lunchtime piano set in Midtown, a no-cost way to catch live music on the way through the city.
